source_status_scope: Historical source-access and locator status under the recorded checking dates and material access limits; not claim support, source truth, complete review or a guarantee of present availability.
scope_note: One entry may bind a paragraph containing several statistics from the same study. This index supplies source navigation and access limits; it does not add scientific claims or certify the underlying publications.

claims.heading: What the evidence supports / Photographs can cue additional reported autobiographical recall
claims.claim: Personal-photo review in nine selected undergraduates elicited additional reported recall, with self-scored outcome and confidence qualifications.
claims.access_limits: Selected primary scoring and outcome sections were checked; full exclusions, supplements, and recomputation were not checked. Same research family does not constitute replication.

claims.heading: What the evidence supports / Photographs can cue additional reported autobiographical recall
claims.claim: An earlier 12-participant review study reported recognition-rating and response-length differences, with response length rather than independently verified correctness as its principal recall measure.
claims.access_limits: One review had full-text extraction and another only search excerpts; no later independent scientific source recheck was performed. The 2026-09-17 follow-up verified bibliographic identity and DOI only.

claims.heading: What the evidence supports / Photographs can cue additional reported autobiographical recall
claims.claim: Personal images elicited additional remembered events and supported timestamp-checkable ordering in young adults, with outcome-specific denominators.
claims.access_limits: Full-text extraction was available to one review route only. Free-recalled event content could not be independently verified, and no later independent primary scoring check was performed.

claims.heading: What the evidence supports / Some procedures improve narrow, checkable outcomes
claims.claim: An accumulated photo sequence improved visited-versus-unvisited discrimination after a guided walking tour in a small all-female sample.
claims.access_limits: Targeted full-text extraction was available, but the primary scoring method was not independently rechecked. This was a narrow occurrence-discrimination task, not ordinary autobiographical free recall.

claims.heading: What the evidence supports / Some procedures improve narrow, checkable outcomes
claims.claim: Photo review after staged witnessed videos supported selected correct-detail outcomes in younger and older adults.
claims.access_limits: The review targeted Experiment 1 rather than the complete publication, and the primary scoring was not independently rechecked. Staged-event evidence does not directly transport to ordinary lived autobiography.

claims.heading: What the evidence supports / Some procedures improve narrow, checkable outcomes
claims.claim: A randomized body-camera review procedure after a simulated theft improved final statement reporting in a mixed-age sample.
claims.access_limits: Participants were aged 17-42; no adult-only subgroup was available. The exact accuracy denominator was unknown, only 10 statements were second-coded, and the setting was virtual reality.

claims.heading: Strongest contrary and complicating evidence
claims.claim: Reactivation combined with related lure exposure increased both target hits and false alarms in younger and older museum-task groups.
claims.access_limits: The primary table was checked, but the strict minimum participant age was unverified and no signal-detection or mechanism reanalysis was performed. The procedure differs from unsuggested personal-photo review.

claims.heading: Strongest contrary and complicating evidence
claims.claim: A genuine class photograph paired with a false childhood narrative and encouraged imagery produced false childhood-event reports.
claims.access_limits: Participant minimum age was unconfirmed in the original scientific review and the reviewed version was an uncorrected proof. The 2026-09-17 follow-up verified bibliographic identity and DOI only.

claims.heading: Strongest contrary and complicating evidence
claims.claim: An altered action video increased belief and memory ratings for staged recent actions in 60 participants aged 18-41.
claims.access_limits: Only primary snippets were available to the original scientific review; the full manuscript was unavailable. The 2026-09-17 follow-up verified the distinct Nash, Wade, and Brewer (2009) bibliographic identity and DOI only.

claims.heading: Strongest contrary and complicating evidence
claims.claim: Flashbulb-memory belief and vividness remained high while narrative consistency declined.
claims.access_limits: One subgroup had a mean age of 17.78, so the sample was not cleanly adult-only. Narrative consistency was not independently verified factual accuracy, and no later independent source recheck was performed.

claims.heading: Strongest contrary and complicating evidence
claims.claim: Reminder-associated updating was positive in one list-learning family and null or nonmatching in other sequence-task families.
claims.access_limits: Original scientific access was partial or abstract-only, and adult minima and robustness were incompletely checked. The 2026-09-17 follow-up verified bibliographic identities and DOIs for the positive Hupbach list-learning study and the Hardwicke, Taqi, and Shanks direct and conceptual replication report only.

claims.heading: Confidence and vividness are not accuracy
claims.claim: An election-memory study compared later recollection with earlier self-report and factual items in a broad adult sample.
claims.access_limits: The extraction targeted Study 1. Study 2 and full emotion-versus-fact dissociation statistics were not comprehensively inspected. Earlier self-report is not objective ground truth for the complete original emotional state.

claims.heading: Human evidence: finite outcomes in specified populations
claims.claim: The LIFE randomized trial reduced major mobility disability over finite follow-up in sedentary older adults with functional limitations.
claims.access_limits: Selected methods and results were independently matched at the reported-design level. No raw-data reanalysis, survival claim, or broad population transport follows.

claims.heading: Human evidence: finite outcomes in specified populations
claims.claim: REHAB-HF supported recovery of measured physical function over three months in older adults hospitalized with heart failure.
claims.access_limits: The result is rehabilitation in a defined impaired population and does not establish general biological-age reversal.

claims.heading: Human evidence: finite outcomes in specified populations
claims.claim: SPRINT reported lower all-cause mortality during finite intervention follow-up in a selected elevated-risk population.
claims.access_limits: Primary access was partial and the safety extraction was incomplete. The endpoint does not uniquely identify general aging-rate modification.

claims.heading: Human evidence: finite outcomes in specified populations
claims.claim: Da Qing reported a finite mortality and survival-area benefit after a lifestyle intervention in adults with impaired glucose tolerance.
claims.access_limits: Cluster design, selected population, ongoing care, and adherence limit generalization. The reported life-year estimate must not be recreated from the hazard ratio.

claims.heading: Human evidence: finite outcomes in specified populations
claims.claim: SELECT reduced its prespecified cardiovascular composite in participants with obesity and established cardiovascular disease.
claims.access_limits: Later mortality estimates were not confirmatory after the hierarchy failed at cardiovascular death, and reviewed safety extraction was incomplete.

claims.heading: Human evidence: finite outcomes in specified populations
claims.claim: ASPREE found no disability-free-survival benefit and found increased major bleeding with aspirin.
claims.access_limits: The null is specific to the tested protocol, endpoint, population, and uncertainty; it is not universal proof of ineffectiveness.

claims.heading: Human evidence: finite outcomes in specified populations
claims.claim: DPPOS detected no mortality benefit over long follow-up for metformin or lifestyle intervention.
claims.access_limits: Treatment convergence and low event rates constrain inference; the result is not proof of exact zero effect.

claims.heading: Human evidence: finite outcomes in specified populations
claims.claim: A later RTB101 trial failed its primary clinical endpoint despite a biological interferon-response signal.
claims.access_limits: The failed primary endpoint constrains this tested protocol and does not establish universal mechanism failure.

claims.heading: Human evidence: finite outcomes in specified populations
claims.claim: Rapamycin plus exercise did not add benefit on the primary chair-stand endpoint and raised a possible interaction concern.
claims.access_limits: The study does not establish universal attenuation or harm.

claims.heading: Human evidence: finite outcomes in specified populations
claims.claim: MASTERS found blunted measured hypertrophic adaptation with metformin during resistance training.
claims.access_limits: Primary access was partial, and consequences for strength or disability were not established.

claims.heading: Animal evidence: stronger lifespan demonstrations, unresolved translation
claims.claim: A three-site genetically heterogeneous mouse study found finite median and upper-tail survival increases with rapamycin.
claims.access_limits: Selected table extraction was checked against a retained document. Upper-tail quantiles are not biological maxima, and shared sites or controls do not independently replicate every schedule or mechanism.

claims.heading: Animal evidence: stronger lifespan demonstrations, unresolved translation
claims.claim: Dietary restriction in diversity-outbred female mice produced a survival signal with lean-mass and immune tradeoffs.
claims.access_limits: Cage-level statistical questions remained open in the original scientific assessment. The 2026-09-17 follow-up verified bibliographic identity and DOI only.

claims.heading: Animal evidence: stronger lifespan demonstrations, unresolved translation
claims.claim: Late-life anti-IL11 treatment produced mouse survival and functional benefits.
claims.access_limits: Independent therapeutic lifespan replication and survival denominator details remained limited in the original scientific assessment. The 2026-09-17 follow-up verified bibliographic identity and DOI only.

claims.heading: Animal evidence: stronger lifespan demonstrations, unresolved translation
claims.claim: Late-life dasatinib plus quercetin was reported to increase median remaining life, not total lifespan.
claims.access_limits: Replication and transport remain limited, and the remaining-life metric must not be promoted into whole-life extension. The 2026-09-17 follow-up verified bibliographic identity and DOI only.

claims.heading: Animal evidence: stronger lifespan demonstrations, unresolved translation
claims.claim: Rhesus-monkey caloric-restriction programs produced discordant survival findings.
claims.access_limits: Feeding, onset age, husbandry, and care are possible explanations rather than a randomized resolution of the discordance.

claims.heading: Animal evidence: stronger lifespan demonstrations, unresolved translation
claims.claim: Specified 2024 Intervention Testing Program schedules produced null findings under their tested conditions.
claims.access_limits: Protocol, dose, onset, exposure, sex, and shared-control limits prevent a universal null inference.

claims.heading: Animal evidence: stronger lifespan demonstrations, unresolved translation
claims.claim: Specified 2026 Intervention Testing Program protocols produced null findings for several compounds.
claims.access_limits: Changed doses, onset, and achieved exposure limit same-protocol refutation and broader generalization.

claims.heading: Animal evidence: stronger lifespan demonstrations, unresolved translation
claims.claim: A preliminary AAV-OSK report in exceptionally old male mice concerned remaining survival rather than whole lifespan.
claims.access_limits: The lifespan paragraph was checked in retained text, but sample, randomization, control, denominator, precision, and supplementary details remained limited. The result was preliminary and unreplicated.

claims.heading: Slowing decline is different from restoring function
claims.claim: Genetically corrected epidermal stem cells regenerated functional epidermis after catastrophic skin loss in one child.
claims.access_limits: This is a local regenerative capability in a pediatric monogenic-disease setting, not direct natural-aging reversal or organism-wide repair.

claims.heading: Slowing decline is different from restoring function
claims.claim: Limbal stem-cell treatment restored renewing corneal epithelium in selected damaged eyes.
claims.access_limits: Methods access was limited, follow-up varied, and local tissue renewal does not establish systemic rejuvenation.

claims.heading: Slowing decline is different from restoring function
claims.claim: An early uncontrolled stem-cell-derived islet study reported one-year endocrine outcomes in 12 full-dose recipients and safety observations in 14 participants.
claims.access_limits: The efficacy and safety populations differ. Total enrollment flow, supplement details, and a later revision difference remained unresolved; later deaths do not explain the denominator split or establish product-caused fatalities.

claims.heading: Slowing decline is different from restoring function
claims.claim: Donor-islet treatment allows bounded repeat administration and carries substantial adverse-reaction and immunosuppression burdens.
claims.access_limits: Finite repeat administration does not establish arbitrary repeat cycles, broad eligibility, or open-ended net safety.

claims.heading: Slowing decline is different from restoring function
claims.claim: Kidney retransplantation after graft failure demonstrates that component replacement can sometimes be repeated.
claims.access_limits: The survival association was observational in selected waitlisted people; causal methods, duration, perioperative burden, general eligibility, and arbitrary-cycle efficacy were not established.

claims.heading: Slowing decline is different from restoring function
claims.claim: Engineered heart muscle supported selected anatomical integration observations in macaques and an early human case.
claims.access_limits: A macaque functional statistic was responder-selected. Perioperative death, rejection after immune withdrawal, and ectopic tissue remain; anatomy does not establish controlled clinical benefit.

claims.heading: Slowing decline is different from restoring function
claims.claim: Nanowarmed rat kidneys supported recipients for 30 days after long-duration organ storage.
claims.access_limits: This is component preservation and life support, not whole-body revival. A 30-day nonsignificant comparison is not equivalence or long-term safety.

claims.heading: Slowing decline is different from restoring function
claims.claim: An older fetal-graft randomized trial found no overall motor benefit despite graft persistence evidence.
claims.access_limits: Primary access was abstract-level. Product era and study context differ from newer graft products; the null remains specific to the tested intervention and endpoint.

claims.heading: Slowing decline is different from restoring function
claims.claim: DREAM-HF reported a null primary clinical endpoint despite a regenerative rationale.
claims.access_limits: The null constrains the tested product and endpoint and does not prove that all regenerative approaches are ineffective.

claims.heading: Slowing decline is different from restoring function
claims.claim: Early modern Parkinson's graft evidence remains uncontrolled or mixed and includes serious treatment-context harm.
claims.access_limits: Placebo effects, medication changes, disease severity, maturation, small samples, and immunosuppression complicate attribution.

claims.heading: Biomarkers are not outcomes
claims.claim: DunedinPACE predicted mortality and cardiovascular outcomes in cohorts separate from its training cohort.
claims.access_limits: This supports prognosis, not treatment-effect surrogacy. Cohort reuse across model analyses limits independence.

claims.heading: Biomarkers are not outcomes
claims.claim: A later clock study supported improved technical reliability.
claims.access_limits: Analytical reliability is distinct from prognosis, intervention response, and treatment-effect clinical surrogacy.

claims.heading: Biomarkers are not outcomes
claims.claim: A randomized CALERIE ancillary analysis found intervention responsiveness for DunedinPACE while other clocks were null.
claims.access_limits: Participant reuse and disagreement among clocks remain. Marker response does not convert clock units into life extension or establish treatment surrogacy.

claims.heading: Biomarkers are not outcomes
claims.claim: An exploratory DO-HEALTH ancillary analysis reported nominal marker-response patterns in 777 selected Swiss participants.
claims.access_limits: There was no single primary clock and no established multiplicity-controlled effect. Long-term survival meaning, timing, selection, and training-overlap questions remained.

claims.heading: Biomarkers are not outcomes
claims.claim: The larger DO-HEALTH parent trial detected no benefit across its six primary clinical outcomes under its specified threshold.
claims.access_limits: The parent and marker analyses used different samples, estimands, sensitivity, and tests. Their contrast neither proves individual-level surrogate failure nor validates surrogacy.
